# 1.2.110 - Rules before 1.3.0, the Monocub's new moves and the dead's own voice room, the stage notes' leftovers, the trial console's steps, and the owner's fixes from the table

Stages E64, E72 (`with` E64) and E91 (`with` E72), one release; with them the E99 line's round 7 and its open-node fix
(e97-98), the gaps-61 line and the gaps-108 line (the owner's items from the table on 1.2.108). Its range is main at
1.2.109 (421f2395; this checkout has no v1.2.109 tag) to the release commit: at 8fc3e798, one hundred and sixty-seven
commits, sixteen of them merges (`git rev-list --count` and `--merges --count` over 421f2395..8fc3e798). Sixty-one are
on the E64 line's branch, 629f52ed to 7ceb4f5c (three merges among them: 34ded63e, 7d916d2c, 4c31eb91), merged as
105765de; seventy-two on the E72 line's branch, 1d411650 to 92559c7d (one merge, 5f46d98f), merged as fa858c3e,
b3b7dff9, e4be9ce3 and 9e00241d; seven on the e97-98 branch, 1f0ebebf to cebe4c69 (one merge, f0b4f9b6), merged as
27bd20ce and 50099632; six on gaps-61, 78ccdde4 to 6de5d2b0 (one merge, 7c0d1af9), merged as ef514e83; nine on
gaps-108, 1adba33b to 2052bf3e, merged as 6e8fd247. Twelve stand on the 1.2.110 line itself (`--first-parent`): those
nine merges, 79ac0c7b, which merges main at 1.2.109, edd02793 (the Spectator guard on the new player rows) and
8fc3e798 (two comments). On top come this file's commit, 1.2.110's ledger rows in tools/stages.json, and the release
commit. In plain words:

- **Clean-up and crisis rules** (E64). The fresh-scene discount holds only while a killing is fresh; no clean-up
  number falls below 8; Tamper costs one action and no Sanity (the killer's own Stage 6 keeps its Sanity price) and
  has no limit a time of day; Wounded costs an action in Daily Life and the Investigation, not in the Class Trial; a
  crisis action aimed at a strong defender is one harder (never the opening roll); a critical can carry a body two
  rooms.
- **Level Up** (E64). No more +1 Health or +1 Sanity picks: a point in Head raises the Sanity maximum, a point in
  Body or Leg the Health maximum. Old picks are brought under the new rule once per world, in a window where the GM
  ticks each change.
- **Other numbers** (E64): Confusion's first tier at 11; a sabotage hit at 12 needs a repair of 2; a trap's victim
  notices it at Night as by day; a Palm steal needs 12. The item draw now shuffles fairly.
- **Observe's critical hint** goes on the finder's own copy only, in a box asked first (E64).
- **The Investigation's GM tools** are tidier (E64): fewer buttons on the bar, Who has what as one table, one word
  "Visibility", shorter hints, and End the chapter, New Remnant and the realization preview fit a 1366x768 screen.
- **The Monocub** (E72). A dead player becomes a Monocub only by accepting the Monocub Rule. Its moves are paid on
  the GM after their checks, capped per student, and its tiles say why they are shut. New: Redeem (free, +1 Hope
  once a game day), Ask for Hope, Tinker, a purse of Hope the GMs keep, Bribe, the GM's Bounty, a move to order, and
  the Ghost Bet. A Monocub sees every room the class found and crosses rooms for free, but not into a running murder's
  room.
- **The dead's voice** (E72): outside the Class Trial a dead student talks in a voice room of their own; the GM can
  move a death kept secret there at once (**Silence now**).
- **Call windows** look like the Action window, and Experience and Ultimate are one tile, **Talent** (E72).
- **The stage notes' leftovers** (E91): the Mastermind can lock their own room and seal a passage at their door; a
  refused Find Passage gives its price back; a student with several owners is treated as owned by each; and smaller
  fixes.
- **The Class Trial console** (E99 round 7): the Verdict, Show summary and End the chapter appear only when they are
  the next step; Start the Final Trial is not offered inside an ordinary trial; the case's ticks belong to one trial.
  On the case map, an open node is its editor, with nothing above it.
- **From the table** (gaps-108, gaps-61): no thin line at the screen's edges while paused; one project in the tray no
  longer fades; folding the tray keeps the blur under the notice tile; the GM button's eye without its tail; a hammer
  for Projects; new glyphs for Hold this ready and Hand this over; the Rest window names the rest; a chat card's glyph
  is readable under Stained Glass.

Nothing in this version ran at a real table or on a Foundry server; what was measured was measured headless, or in
Chromium on the module's own harness pages (the module's stylesheets, not Foundry's). Below, an R number names one of
the module's own tests (`game.drpg.runTests()`), and a scenario one of the headless harness's multi-browser runs.

## Before installing

- **Rules change in a running season** (E64): the numbers above apply from the update. Several are defaults the
  owner has not confirmed (docs/dev/e64/STATUS.md marks each).
- **The Level Up migration** (E64, 7242cce0, 4f41bf90): once per world, on the primary GM's load, a window lists each
  student whose past +1 Health or +1 Sanity picks or Head, Body or Leg points change under the new rule, one box each.
  Apply writes the ticked ones; Cancel asks again next load. Only a sheet the module set up (with the season's stamp)
  is read. New world setting `levelUpsMigrated` marks it done.
- **Two more migrations** (E72 C2, E91 C8): the crime witness's mark moves off the actor flag into the GMs' Monocub
  record (`liftCubWitness`), and old rest stamps with no chapter are given one or dropped (`chapterRestStamps`). Both
  carry `since: "1.2.110"` in migrate.mjs, the version they ship in (29056048; their lines had planned 1.2.117).
- **A Monocub is made by its player** (E72 C6): the old Monocubs window is gone (`game.drpg.monocubDialog` opens the
  Students window); the GM sends an invitation and the player accepts the Rule.
- **New world settings, GMs' stores**: `gmCubs`, `mineCubs`, `gmCubTargets`, `gmBounties`, `gmProjectWork` (E72).
- **New bridge actions**: `monocub.answer`, `bribe.offer`, `bribe.answer` (E72), `mastermind.lairLock`,
  `passage.lairSeal` (E91); each refuses a Spectator (edd02793).
- **Voice** (E72 C8): a dead student outside the trial is sent a room of their own account (`drpg-dead-<userId>`),
  not the main room; nothing is written on the user. In the trial nothing changes.
- **Two known leaks recorded** (audit/harness/known-leaks.json): `foundry-cub-purse` (a Monocub's move with no Hope
  drop on its sheet tells a console its purse paid) and TR30 kept as a Foundry limit (a trial's list of muted dead is
  in the user documents every browser holds). The README says both.
- **Texts**: lang/en.json holds 5289 keys and lang/pl.json 6322 (1.2.109: 5141 English); the handbooks in both
  languages carry the new rules, the Monocub and the console's steps.
- **`module.json`**: unchanged but for the version. Foundry `verified` 14.365, Daggerheart `verified` 2.6.5.

## Fixed from the owner's table on 1.2.109

- **The day's boards on the clock on the curtain** (ecba2870; tests renumbered in 6884344d): ending the Morning
  Eclipse from the curtain clock's right chevron or the panel's Eclipse button now plays the end-of-day board, then the
  start-of-day board. Next time of day from Night still plays them, and so does the chapter end's next morning, after
  the trial's exit. Edit campaign's day + 1 plays nothing: it is a correction. On the Eclipse's road the Night's
  summary is no longer shown twice: it folds into the board at the Morning Eclipse's start. A Night to Morning moved by
  hand plays no board and keeps its summary. The clock has a new field, `dayBoard` (null by default), written only by
  a real roll-over and the chapter end's next morning. Tests, each red at 1ff4bc77: R4400 and R4401 (tier 1), tier 2
  "E110 day boards A" (the Eclipse's road) and "E110 day boards B" (Edit campaign silent, Next still plays), scenario
  93 "road" (p1 and the Spectator start the board). R3724 gained two cases (red at 1ff4bc77); R3715's clocks carry the
  stamp.
- **The boards' frame** (c5334f00): the boards wear the frame of the module's ordinary windows in both themes; it was
  the trial band's pink (red under Monokuma Legacy). The band and the "spilling" mood word keep that colour. R4402, red
  at 1ff4bc77.
- **End the chapter's flag** (70e672d8, 8ee4391d): in Season setup and Edit campaign under Stained Glass the flag
  stands before the word; it covered the "E". The rule is the glyph generator's (scripts/tests-glyphs.mjs, written by
  tools/glyph-map.mjs). R4403, red at 1ff4bc77. Shots on a harness page in Chromium, not Foundry.
- **The migrations' `since`** (29056048): `liftCubWitness` and `chapterRestStamps` carry 1.2.110, the version they
  ship in. R178 and R3814 pin it, both red at 1ff4bc77.
- **Wide project windows on by default** (d12ff689; the owner, 13.11.2026): Create a project, Edit project and
  Propose a project open wide unless a browser turns the setting off; one that saved its own choice keeps it. The
  handbooks say so. R4404, red at 1ff4bc77.
